services.hero_description: Creosote, soot, and debris can restrict airflow and increase fire risk. Our professional sweeping service thoroughly cleans masonry and prefabricated chimneys while keeping your home protected throughout the process.
services.whatsincluded_1_body: We clear all stages of creosote buildup from your flue walls using professional grade brushes and vacuum equipment.
services.whatsincluded_2_body: We clean the firebox and smoke chamber thoroughly so your system drafts cleanly from bottom to top.
services.whatsincluded_3_body: Leaves, animal nesting, and other obstructions inside the flue are removed completely.
services.whatsincluded_4_body: After every sweep we give you a brief condition update and flag anything that needs attention.
services.signs_1_title: You burn wood regularly through the season
services.signs_1_body: If you use your fireplace more than a few times a month, an annual sweep is the minimum. Heavy users should sweep every season.
services.signs_2_title: You see thick black flaking inside the flue or firebox
services.signs_2_body: Flaking black deposits are a sign of Stage 2 or Stage 3 creosote — a serious fire hazard that needs immediate professional removal.
services.signs_3_title: You smell a strong smoky or tarry odor even when the fireplace isn't in use
services.signs_3_body: Persistent odor between fires usually means heavy creosote accumulation. This is a moderate warning sign that a sweep is overdue.
services.signs_4_title: It's been more than 12 months since your last cleaning
services.signs_4_body: Even light users should sweep annually. Time-based buildup happens regardless of how often you burn.
services.h1: Let's clear out what's been building up in your chimney

services.hero_description: Cracked mortar, damaged firebrick, deteriorated refractory panels, and worn fireboxes can compromise both safety and appearance. Our team provides careful repairs and restoration for masonry and prefabricated fireplaces.
services.whatsincluded_1_body: We replace damaged refractory panels with correctly sized, high temperature rated units.
services.whatsincluded_2_body: We repoint failing mortar joints with refractory mortar rated for direct flame exposure.
services.whatsincluded_3_body: We repair spalled or cracked firebox flooring with appropriate refractory materials.
services.whatsincluded_4_body: We parge the smoke chamber smooth to improve draft efficiency and reduce creosote buildup.
services.signs_1_title: You see visible cracks in the firebox walls or floor
services.signs_1_body: Any crack in the firebox interior is a safety issue. Heat and gases can pass through cracks into surrounding structure. Stop use and schedule repair.
services.signs_2_title: The refractory panels have deep gouges, chunks missing, or are separating at the seams
services.signs_2_body: Panel failure is one of the most urgent fireplace repairs. This is the barrier between fire and your home's framing — it cannot be deferred.
services.signs_3_title: Mortar between firebox bricks is soft, crumbling, or falling out
services.signs_3_body: Deteriorating mortar in a firebox is a moderate but time-sensitive issue. It will worsen with every fire and should be addressed before the next season.
services.signs_4_title: You've repaired the same area more than once in recent years
services.signs_4_body: Recurring issues in the same spot may indicate a deeper structural or moisture problem. Worth a full evaluation rather than another spot fix.

services.hero_description: Get a clear understanding of your chimney’s condition. We evaluate masonry and prefabricated systems for buildup, leaks, deterioration, venting concerns, and other problems before they become expensive repairs.
services.whatsincluded_1_body: We inspect the firebox walls, floor, and damper for cracks, spalling, or deteriorating mortar.
services.whatsincluded_2_body: We assess the full flue and liner for obstructions, buildup, or damage that could restrict airflow.
services.whatsincluded_3_body: We check the crown and cap for cracks or missing components that leave your system exposed to water.
services.whatsincluded_4_body: Every inspection ends with a clear written summary of findings and honest recommendations.
services.signs_1_title: It's been over a year since your last inspection
services.signs_1_body: Annual inspections are the baseline for chimney safety. If you can't remember the last one, it's time.
services.signs_2_title: You've noticed cracks in your firebox or exterior masonry
services.signs_2_body: Visible cracks can indicate serious structural movement or water damage. This warrants an immediate inspection before any use.
services.signs_3_title: You're seeing smoke enter the room when the fireplace is in use
services.signs_3_body: Smoke backdraft suggests a blockage, liner failure, or draft issue. Stop use and schedule an inspection right away.
services.signs_4_title: You recently bought the home or haven't used the fireplace in years
services.signs_4_body: Unknown history means unknown risk. A fresh inspection is the only way to know what you're working with.
services.h1: Let's get your chimney safe and ready for the winter

services.hero_description: Protect the top of your chimney with a properly fitted solution. We install standard flue caps, spark arrestors, and custom full-coverage caps designed to block rain, debris, birds, and other animals.
services.whatsincluded_1_body: We measure your flue opening precisely and select a cap that fits correctly every time.
services.whatsincluded_2_body: We install durable galvanized steel caps as standard with stainless and copper available for homes where aesthetics matter.
services.whatsincluded_3_body: Every cap includes a mesh skirt that blocks birds, squirrels, and raccoons from nesting in your flue.
services.whatsincluded_4_body: Caps are secured with stainless screws and sealed at the base to keep water out in any weather.
services.signs_1_title: You don't currently have a cap — or you're not sure
services.signs_1_body: If your chimney has no cap, every rainstorm is sending water directly into your flue. This is the single easiest fix with the highest protective value.
services.signs_2_title: An animal has gotten into your chimney or fireplace
services.signs_2_body: If something has already gotten in, your cap is missing or failed. This needs to be addressed immediately — animals can become trapped and create serious hazards.
services.signs_3_title: You're finding debris, leaves, or nesting material in the firebox
services.signs_3_body: Debris falling into the firebox is a clear sign the flue is open and unprotected. A cap resolves this completely.
services.signs_4_title: Your existing cap is rusted, bent, or sitting loose
services.signs_4_body: A damaged cap provides little protection. If it's visibly degraded or shifting in the wind, replacement is overdue.
services.h1: Let's keep rain, animals, and debris out of your chimney

services.hero_description: Routine care helps your fireplace operate reliably when temperatures drop. We inspect, clean, and maintain critical components to catch deterioration early and reduce the likelihood of unexpected problems.
services.whatsincluded_1_body: Every visit starts with a full top to bottom inspection and clean of the firebox, damper, and flue.
services.whatsincluded_2_body: We service the damper hardware so it operates smoothly and seals fully for better efficiency.
services.whatsincluded_3_body: We check door gaskets and seals for compression loss and replace them where needed.
services.whatsincluded_4_body: We document any developing issues and give you a clear picture of what to watch going forward.
services.signs_1_title: You schedule an annual service on most other home systems but not the fireplace
services.signs_1_body: HVAC, water heater, gutters — most homeowners maintain these annually. The fireplace deserves the same cadence.
services.signs_2_title: The fireplace seems to be burning less efficiently than it used to
services.signs_2_body: Reduced performance — more smoke, less heat, harder to start — often signals multiple small issues accumulating. A maintenance visit diagnoses and resolves them.
services.signs_3_title: You're noticing small issues but nothing dramatic enough to call for repair
services.signs_3_body: This is exactly the right time for maintenance. Catching developing issues early is always cheaper than waiting for a failure.
services.signs_4_title: You want confidence heading into the burning season
services.signs_4_body: A pre-season maintenance visit is the cleanest way to start fall and winter knowing your fireplace is fully ready.
services.h1: Let's take care of your fireplace so it's always ready to use

services.hero_description: Pilot won’t light, flame looks weak, or the remote stopped responding? We diagnose ignition systems, burners, gas logs, controls, and related components to identify the correct repair or replacement.
services.whatsincluded_1_body: We clean and test the pilot assembly, thermocouple, and igniter to resolve most ignition failures.
services.whatsincluded_2_body: We clean the burner and orifice to restore proper combustion and even flame output.
services.whatsincluded_3_body: We test the gas valve for correct operation and verify inlet pressure is within spec.
services.whatsincluded_4_body: We reposition or replace ceramic logs and media to restore the original look and flame pattern.
services.signs_1_title: The pilot light goes out repeatedly or won't stay lit
services.signs_1_body: A pilot that won't hold is usually a thermocouple issue — a routine repair. But it should be addressed before continued use, as a failed thermocouple is a safety control.
services.signs_2_title: The unit won't ignite at all
services.signs_2_body: Complete ignition failure could mean a gas valve issue, wiring fault, or control board failure. This needs a diagnostic before any further attempts to light.
services.signs_3_title: The flame is yellow, uneven, or significantly smaller than it used to be
services.signs_3_body: Flame quality issues indicate a burner or gas supply problem. Yellow flames in particular signal incomplete combustion — a moderate concern that warrants prompt service.
services.signs_4_title: You smell gas near the fireplace even when it's off
services.signs_4_body: Any gas smell when the unit is off is an urgent safety issue. Do not attempt to use the fireplace. Ventilate the area and call for service immediately.

services.hero_description: Know what’s happening inside your fireplace before lighting it. We examine the firebox, damper, venting, refractory panels, burner components, and surrounding structure for damage and potential safety concerns.
services.whatsincluded_1_body: We examine the firebox interior for cracks or heat damage that could allow gases to reach surrounding framing.
services.whatsincluded_2_body: We test the damper operation and seal, and note if repair or replacement would benefit you.
services.whatsincluded_3_body: We inspect the smoke chamber for damage that could compromise draft performance or safety.
services.whatsincluded_4_body: We check the hearth extension and surround for proper clearance and signs of heat damage.
services.signs_1_title: You haven't had the fireplace inspected since moving in
services.signs_1_body: Previous owners may have used it heavily or made modifications. You have no way to know the condition without an inspection.
services.signs_2_title: The damper feels stiff, sticky, or won't fully close
services.signs_2_body: Damper issues can mean warping from heat, rust, or debris obstruction. A fully stuck damper needs immediate attention before use.
services.signs_3_title: You notice a musty or smoky smell coming from the fireplace when it's closed
services.signs_3_body: Odor with the damper closed suggests the seal is failing and outside air — along with whatever is in the flue — is entering your living space.
services.signs_4_title: The fireplace hasn't been used in multiple years
services.signs_4_body: Inactivity doesn't mean safe. Moisture, pests, and slow material degradation happen regardless of use. Inspect before restarting.

services.hero_description: Bring back a cleaner, more inviting fireplace without covering your home in soot. We carefully remove ash, loose buildup, staining, and debris while protecting the surrounding floors and living space.
services.whatsincluded_1_body: We remove all ash, soot, and debris from the firebox using HEPA filtered equipment.
services.whatsincluded_2_body: Glass doors are cleaned inside and out with non abrasive products that restore clarity without scratching.
services.whatsincluded_3_body: We brush the full smoke chamber and vacuum all loosened material before it falls back into the firebox.
services.whatsincluded_4_body: We clear soot and debris from the damper and throat area to restore proper airflow.
services.signs_1_title: The glass doors are heavily blackened and you can't see through them
services.signs_1_body: Opaque glass is a sign of incomplete combustion or poor airflow — worth cleaning and then noting whether the issue recurs.
services.signs_2_title: There's a heavy ash and soot smell even when the fireplace isn't running
services.signs_2_body: Lingering odor between uses suggests significant buildup in the firebox or smoke chamber that needs to be cleared out.
services.signs_3_title: Ash has been sitting in the firebox for more than one season
services.signs_3_body: Old ash absorbs moisture and becomes mildly acidic. Letting it sit long-term accelerates firebox floor and wall degradation.
services.signs_4_title: You're heading into or out of burning season
services.signs_4_body: A clean fireplace at the start of the season performs better and gives you a fresh baseline. At the end of the season, cleaning prevents off-season moisture damage.

services.hero_description: From masonry and mortar to siding, trim, crowns, flashing, and complete rebuilds, we’ve got your chimney covered with repairs tailored to its construction, condition, and long-term needs.
services.whatsincluded_1_body: Deteriorated mortar joints are ground out and replaced to restore structural integrity and stop water penetration.
services.whatsincluded_2_body: We remove damaged bricks and replace them with matching units so the repair holds structurally and looks clean.
services.whatsincluded_3_body: We reseal or replace the flashing at your roofline to stop water intrusion at the source.
services.whatsincluded_4_body: We repair the crown and apply a waterproof sealant to prevent future water damage.
services.signs_1_title: You notice water stains on the ceiling or wall near the fireplace
services.signs_1_body: Water intrusion near the chimney almost always points to flashing failure or a cracked crown. This needs repair before the next rain season.
services.signs_2_title: You see white staining (efflorescence) on the exterior masonry
services.signs_2_body: White mineral deposits on brick are a sign that water is actively moving through your chimney structure. Left alone, this accelerates deterioration rapidly.
services.signs_3_title: Bricks or mortar are visibly crumbling or missing
services.signs_3_body: Physical loss of masonry material is a serious structural concern. This should be addressed immediately — the damage compounds with every freeze cycle.
services.signs_4_title: The chimney looks slightly different than it used to — settling or leaning
services.signs_4_body: Gradual movement in the chimney structure can signal foundation or footing issues. Worth a professional eye sooner rather than later.
